title: Classic Lasagna
metaDescription: Classic beef lasagna with layers of meat sauce, ricotta and melted mozzarella — the ultimate baked pasta comfort dinner.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: classic lasagna, homemade lasagna, beef lasagna recipe

steps.name: Make the meat sauce
steps.text: Brown the ground beef with onion and garlic, about 7 minutes. Drain fat, stir in marinara sauce, and simmer 10 minutes.

steps.name: Cook the noodles
steps.text: Cook lasagna noodles according to package directions until al dente. Drain and lay flat to prevent sticking.

steps.name: Mix the ricotta filling
steps.text: Combine ricotta, egg, parsley, salt and pepper in a bowl.

steps.name: Layer
steps.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). In a 9x13-inch dish, layer meat sauce, noodles, ricotta mixture and mozzarella, repeating for 3 layers. Top with remaining mozzarella and parmesan.

steps.name: Bake
steps.text: Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 15-20 more minutes until bubbly and golden. Rest 10-15 minutes before slicing.

tips.question: Why does my lasagna fall apart when sliced?
tips.answer: Cutting it too soon is the most common cause — lasagna needs 10-15 minutes to rest after baking so the layers set enough to hold together when sliced.

tips.question: Do I need to pre-cook the noodles if using regular ones?
tips.answer: Regular lasagna noodles should be cooked to al dente first — oven-ready/no-boil noodles skip this step but need extra sauce moisture to soften properly while baking.

tips.question: Can I assemble this ahead and bake later?
tips.answer: Yes — assemble fully, cover, and refrigerate up to 24 hours. Add about 10-15 extra minutes to the covered bake time if going in cold.

storyIntro: Lasagna has a reputation as a weekend project, and the layering does take some time, but nothing about it is actually difficult — it's just assembly.
The one rule worth following closely: let it rest before cutting, or the first slice will collapse into a puddle of sauce.
storyNote: Let the lasagna rest for a full 10-15 minutes after baking before cutting — this is what allows the layers to set and hold their shape instead of sliding apart on the plate.
